transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
I came in because I barely care about the things I used to enjoy. Dance class, hiking, trying new recipes, even game night—they all just feel like chores now, and I keep putting them off.
Have there been times when you felt unusually energetic or wired for several days in a row?
No, I haven’t really noticed anything like that.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?
Yeah. Most days I have this low, sour feeling underneath everything—like fear and guilt, even when nothing bad is happening.
Have you been hearing voices that other people can’t hear?
No, I haven’t noticed hearing voices that other people can’t hear.
Have you been feeling this low mood most days for at least two years?
Yes. It started after the robbery at my festival job, about two years and three months ago, and it’s been there most days since then.
Do you feel your low mood has stayed closely connected to the robbery that happened at your festival job?
Yeah, I think so. Ever since then, most days I’ve had this low, sour feeling underneath everything—fear and guilt—even when nothing bad is happening.
Did your low mood start within three months after the robbery?
Yes, it started after the robbery—about two years and three months ago.
Have these feelings been causing problems in your work or daily life?

Yeah. I’ve missed Chamber application deadlines, and I keep putting my catering plans off because I just can’t handle the paperwork, jobs, and people reliably like I used to. I see my friends less too. My life’s gotten smaller around what feels safe.
Do you ever have sudden surges of intense fear when you’re in crowds or in places that remind you of the robbery?
Sometimes, yeah. If a cash box snaps shut, or someone comes up behind me in a kitchen, it hits me really fast. I can hear the voices again and my stomach just drops, like it’s happening right then.
Have you had a noticeable change in your appetite?
I haven’t really noticed a clear change in my appetite.
Do you have unwanted memories of the robbery that pop into your mind when you don’t want them to?

Yeah, sometimes. A cash box snapping shut, or somebody coming up behind me in a kitchen, can bring it all back really fast. I hear the voices again and my stomach drops like it’s happening right then.
Do you go out of your way to avoid places, conversations, or activities that remind you of the robbery?
Yeah. I turn down festival jobs, evening deliveries, and some shared kitchens because I don’t want to be reminded of that night or have that panic start up.
Since the robbery, have you been unusually jumpy or easily startled?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed myself being especially jumpy.
Have you been having nightmares about the robbery?
I don’t think so. I haven’t noticed dreams about it.
Since the robbery, have you often blamed yourself for what happened?
Yeah. I keep thinking I should’ve known better than to take that booking. And I feel like I failed the people who were helping me—I didn’t keep them safe.
Since the robbery, have you often felt on guard or watchful, even when you were safe?
Yeah, especially in parking lots or when I’m picking something up. I’m always checking who’s around me, where my car is, and how quickly I could leave, even when everyone else seems relaxed.
Do you ever feel as if the robbery is happening again in the moment, not just that you remember it?
Sometimes, yeah. Like if a cash box snaps shut, or someone comes up behind me in a kitchen, it hits me really fast. I can hear the voices again and my stomach drops like it’s happening right then.
Since the robbery, have you often felt detached or cut off from other people?

Yeah. I still answer my friends sometimes, but when I’m with them, I feel sort of far away, like I’m watching everything from a distance. I don’t really know how to get back to feeling close to them like I did before.
Since the robbery, have you often felt that the world is unsafe or that other people can’t be trusted?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed feeling that way all the time.
Since the robbery, have you often had trouble sleeping?
I’m not sure I’ve noticed trouble sleeping, no.
